title: Burst-budgeted Quantile Autoscaling Engine with Shadow Simulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a conservative, tenant-aware autoscaling policy engine that meets throughput guarantees while allowing controlled short bursts. The engine must provide transparent, reproducible scaling decisions (simulator/shadow mode), be KV-cache and batching aware, and honor per-tenant safety limits and SKU capacity ceilings.

Background: Current autoscalers either react too slowly to sudden traffic bursts (causing 95th/99th latency violations) or overshoot capacity and drive cost spikes. We want a policy that: (1) aims at a percentile-based latency/throughput target, (2) allows short bursts via a token-bucket style budget, and (3) enforces multi-dimensional safety fences (max replicas by SKU, cooldowns, error-rate gating, and debt repayment on budget use).

Key concepts / components:
- Target metric composition: combined metric = max(quantile(Q_short, window_short), EWMA_throughput(window_long) * headroom_factor). Default Q_short=95 over 60s, window_long=10m. This ensures responsiveness to spikes while preventing knee-jerk scaling on transient noise.
- Burst budget (token bucket): each tenant has a burst budget measured in effective QPS-equivalent tokens. Using the budget permits temporary capacity above baseline for short durations. Budget accrual rate = committed_throughput * budget_fraction (configurable per contract). Budget cannot be negative beyond a bounded debt cap. Debt triggers stricter down-scaling and longer repayment windows.
- Slew limiter and step caps: per-scale-step limit expressed as fraction of current capacity (default 25%/step) and absolute replica delta cap per 30s.
- Safety fences: SKU_max_replicas, global_fleet_allocation_percent (prevents one tenant from starving others), error_rate_gate (disallow scale-down if 5xx or model-level rejection rate rises > threshold), and time-based rollback gates.
- KV-cache and batching awareness: scale decisions factor in effective throughput gain from cached prefixes and batching windows. For models with high cache-hit rates, scale by requests rather than tokens to avoid overprovisioning.
- Policy DSL: small declarative language to express rules (targets, limits, exceptions); will be compiled to runtime plans and exposed in console for inspection.
- Shadow simulator: an offline / streaming simulator that runs policies against historical traces and a production shadow mode that emits proposed actions without mutating fleet. Simulator will produce a diff view, cost/latency forecast, and violation cases for policy tuning.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Quantile-based target vs mean: quantiles protect tail SLAs. We accept slightly higher steady-state cost to avoid 99th/95th latency regressions.
- Burst budgets introduce complexity (tracking, debt): but they are necessary for PLG customers with spiky traffic. Budget debt has explicit repayment to avoid persistent overcommit.
- Conservative default safety: defaults favor stability; aggressive tuning is opt-in per customer/contract.

Acceptance criteria (AC):
1) Autoscaler implements the combined metric calculator and produces deterministic scale decisions for recorded traces.
2) Burst budget semantics implemented: accrual, consumption, debt accounting, and constraints respected.
3) Safety fences enforced: SKU caps, error-rate gates, and global allocation limits tested.
4) Simulator: can replay 30 days of traffic for a tenant and produce a report with expected cost delta, percentile latency delta, and highlight any policy-induced SLA violations.
5) Shadow mode deployed to 10% of production tenants: logs proposed actions, no mutation, and exposes false-positive/negative cases.
6) Dashboard: per-tenant policy summary, recent scale actions, budget balance timeline, and a simulator comparison view.
7) Unit + integration tests covering edge cases (zero-traffic, sustained surge, burst-debt-followed-by-low-traffic).

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1-2: Policy DSL + metric composer implementation; unit tests for composition. (Spike: evaluate quantile estimator libraries.)
- Week 3: Burst budget service + debt accounting API; DB schema for per-tenant budgets.
- Week 4: Integrate KV-cache signals and batching modifiers; local offline simulator skeleton.
- Week 5: Safety fence enforcer; step caps and cooldowns; end-to-end integration tests against synthetic traces.
- Week 6: Shadow mode rollout to internal tenants; dashboard components for inspection.
- Week 7-8: Canaried production rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with close telemetry and rollback playbook.

Telemetry and alerts (initial set):
- Metrics: proposed_scale_actions, enacted_scale_actions, budget_tokens, budget_debt, scale_failure_count, scale_latency_ms, ingress_qps, effective_qps_after_cache, model_95th_latency.
- Alerts: sustained budget_debt > 5m (warn), scale_action_fail_rate > 1% (pager), produced_action_vs_enacted_discrepancy > 10% (pager), 95th latency delta > SLA (pager).

Rollout and safety plan:
- Start in shadow mode for internal and non-critical tenants. Collect simulator vs actual metrics for 2 weeks.
- Enable canary for low-traffic tenants with manual ops approval. Holdback policy for any tenant where average budget_debt > threshold.
- Automated rollback: if enacted actions cause error rates to rise or if cost delta > configured threshold, a circuit breaker stops autoscaler for impacted tenant for configurable cooldown.

Open questions / risks:
- Determining conservative defaults for budget fractions and debt caps that work across SKU mix.
- How to attribute KV-cache benefits across tenants when shared caches exist.
- Long-term storage and TTL for budget accounting (how long to keep debt history).
